question: The Budhabalanga and Baitarini rivers have their source in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Budhabalanga River-

 
 
• The Budhabalanga, meaning old Balanga, rises in the Similipal hills and plunges through Barehipani Falls, the second-highest, located in Simlipal National Park.
 
• It then flows in a northerly direction up to the village Karanjiapal in Bangiriposi police station.
 
• Thereafter, it turns to the northeast and flows along the railway track up to the village of Jhankapahadi.
 
• There it changes its course to the south and meets the Katra Nala.
 
• The other tributaries are the Palpala and the Chipat, which are hill streams rising from the Similipal hills.
 
• Then the river passes through Baripada.
 
• It later flows through the Balasore district and into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• ** Baitarini **
 
 
• The Baitarani River is the second-largest tributary of the Brahmani River.
 
• It originates from the Gonasika hills in Kendujhar district of Odisha and flows for about 360 kilometers (220 miles) before joining the Brahmani River near Dhamra.
 
• It flows through the districts of Keonjhar, Bhadrak, Mayurbhanj, and Balasore.
 
• The Baitarani originates from the Gonasika/Guptaganga (Cow Nose Shaped) hills, and starts flowing over a stone looking like the nostril of a cow.
 
• Since water gets out of a structure that looks like the nose of a cow, the hill has been named accordingly.
 
• Afterwards for about half a kilometre the river flows underground and is not visible from outside.
 
• The Baitarani is known here by the name Guptaganga or the Gupta Baitarani, in Gonasika of Keonjhar district in Odisha.
 
• River Baitarani is also termed as the Ganga of Odisha. 
 
• The mythologically important Gonasika hill is situated at a distance of 30 km form Keonjhar town.
 
• Hundreds of devotees visit this place everyday to witness the Baitarani River as well as the Lord Mahadev temple.
